Normal distribution functions

Source: R/normal.R
normal-functions.Rd

The standard normal distribution's functions as scipy.special computes them, for code that needs SciPy's values rather than a distribution family.

Usage

sc_ndtr(x)

sc_log_ndtr(x)

sc_ndtri(p)

sc_ndtri_exp(y)

sc_owens_t(h, a)

Arguments

x

Numeric or complex vector.

p

Numeric vector of probabilities.

y

Numeric vector of log probabilities (at most 0).

h, a

Numeric vectors.

Value

A double vector, or a complex vector for complex input.

Details

  • sc_ndtr(): the cumulative distribution function \(\Phi(x)\), complex. Base R: pnorm().

  • sc_log_ndtr(): \(\log \Phi(x)\), accurate far into the lower tail, complex. Base R: pnorm(x, log.p = TRUE).

  • sc_ndtri(): the quantile function, the inverse of sc_ndtr(). Base R: qnorm().

  • sc_ndtri_exp(): the inverse of sc_log_ndtr(), for log probabilities too small for exp(). Base R: qnorm(y, log.p = TRUE).

  • sc_owens_t(): Owen's T function \(T(h, a)\), which gives bivariate and skew-normal probabilities.

Arguments are recycled, NA gives NA, and the result takes its dimensions, or else its names, from the arguments as base R arithmetic does; see sc_seterr() for the conditions the kernels raise.

See also

https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/special.html#gaussian-normal-distribution

Examples

sc_ndtr(c(-1, 0, 1))
#> [1] 0.1586553 0.5000000 0.8413447
sc_log_ndtr(-40)
#> [1] -804.6084
sc_ndtri(0.975)
#> [1] 1.959964
sc_ndtri_exp(-1000)
#> [1] -44.61575
sc_owens_t(0.5, 2)
#> [1] 0.1415806
